sources.title: Inside the government’s racial bias case against Donald Trump’s company, and how he fought it
FBI releases file on 1970s Trump housing discrimination case

supported_event_claim: The Justice Department sued Trump Management in 1973 over alleged racial discrimination in rental housing; Donald and Fred Trump settled in 1975 without admitting wrongdoing under terms requiring anti-discrimination measures.
reason: Contemporaneous government case details and later reporting support the lawsuit and settlement. The coded application evidence is described in government interview accounts; the settlement was not an admission.

sources.title: DEADLY DONALD

supported_event_claim: After the Central Park jogger assault, Trump bought full-page ads in four New York newspapers urging reinstatement of the death penalty.
reason: UPI’s contemporaneous report directly describes the ads. The supplied synopsis’s precise $85,000 amount is not established by this source.

sources.title: Trump admits Obama was born in U.S., but falsely blames Clinton for starting rumors

supported_event_claim: Trump promoted doubts about Barack Obama’s birthplace for years and acknowledged in September 2016 that Obama was born in the United States.
reason: The report documents the long-running claims and the 2016 reversal. It supports the conduct but does not itself establish the entry’s broad causal description of Trump’s political career.

sources.title: Superseding indictment, United States v. Trump, Nauta, and De Oliveira
Trump classified documents at Mar-a-Lago

supported_event_claim: The federal indictment alleged that after leaving office Trump retained hundreds of classified documents at Mar-a-Lago, including documents concerning nuclear programs and defense capabilities, without authorization.
reason: The indictment directly supports the alleged retention and its contents. These are allegations in a charging document; the entry’s characterization as established theft is not adopted here.

sources.title: Executive Order 13769—Protecting the Nation From Foreign Terrorist Entry Into the United States
sources.publisher: Office of the Federal Register, National Archives and Records Administration

sources.title: Administration of Donald J. Trump, 2017: Executive Order 13769 description
sources.publisher: Office of the Federal Register, National Archives and Records Administration

supported_event_claim: On January 27, 2017, Trump issued Executive Order 13769, which suspended entry for 90 days for nationals of seven designated countries, including six Muslim-majority countries.
reason: The order and official presidential compilation document the action. The entry’s phrase ‘banning entry’ is a simplified description of the order’s scope and exceptions.

sources.title: Miss USA Contestant: Donald Trump Walked in on Naked Women in Dressing Room
The allegations about Donald Trump and Miss Teen USA contestants

supported_event_claim: Former pageant contestants reported that Trump entered contestants’ dressing areas while they were changing; Trump also described entering backstage areas in a 2005 interview.
reason: The sources distinguish contestants’ allegations from Trump’s recorded account. The packet’s characterization of routine predatory conduct and the full 1996–2016 span are broader than these sources establish.

sources.title: Trump dined with Kanye West and white nationalist Nick Fuentes, adviser says
Trump criticized for dining with far-right activist Nick Fuentes and rapper Ye

supported_event_claim: Trump hosted a November 22, 2022 dinner at Mar-a-Lago attended by Kanye West and Nick Fuentes; Fuentes has promoted antisemitic conspiracy theories and has been described by credible sources as a white nationalist or white supremacist.
reason: CBS and The Washington Post independently report the dinner and identify the attendees. The record does not establish that Trump knowingly invited Fuentes.

sources.title: Inside the government’s racial bias case against Donald Trump’s company, and how he fought it
FBI releases file on 1970s Trump housing discrimination case

supported_event_claim: The Justice Department filed a 1973 housing discrimination suit against Trump Management, alleging discriminatory rental practices; the Trumps settled in 1975 without admitting wrongdoing.
reason: Credible reporting documents the case and settlement. The packet’s placeholder DOJ and settlement links are not sources, and no tenant testimony records were linked in the packet.

sources.title: Trump again uses racially insensitive term to describe coronavirus
The Federal Response to Anti-Asian Racism in the United States

supported_event_claim: Trump used ‘kung flu’ to refer to COVID-19 at public events in June 2020; the U.S. Commission on Civil Rights documents concerns that racialized pandemic terminology could stigmatize Asian communities.
reason: Sources establish the phrase and documented concern about stigmatizing effects, but do not establish that this phrase caused particular hate crimes or quantify its effect.

sources.title: Tweets of May 31, 2017
sources.publisher: The American Presidency Project, UC Santa Barbara

sources.title: Trump targets ‘negative press covfefe’ in garbled midnight tweet that becomes worldwide joke

supported_event_claim: Trump posted ‘Despite the constant negative press covfefe’ shortly after midnight on May 31, 2017; the post was deleted several hours later and he joked about its meaning in a follow-up tweet.
reason: The American Presidency Project archives the tweets and timestamps; The Washington Post reports the deletion and reaction. The record’s claim that the meaning was never clarified is not necessary to establish the event.

sources.title: Trump watches eclipse from White House
NASA Recommends Safety Tips to View the August Solar Eclipse

supported_event_claim: Trump was photographed briefly looking toward the partially eclipsed sun without protective eyewear while viewing the 2017 eclipse; NASA warned that looking directly at the sun can damage vision.
reason: CBS/AP reports the brief glance and that Trump wore glasses for most of the viewing; NASA provides the safety guidance. The packet overstates the duration as sustained looking.

sources.title: Michael Cohen Pleads Guilty in Manhattan Federal Court to Eight Counts, Including Criminal Tax Evasion and Campaign Finance Violations
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Southern District of New York

sources.title: Trump hush money trial: A timeline of key events in the case

supported_event_claim: Michael Cohen wired approximately $130,000 to Stormy Daniels’s attorney on October 27, 2016, as part of an agreement to suppress her story before the election; Cohen later pleaded guilty to campaign-finance violations related to the payment.
reason: The DOJ record and AP timeline support the transfer and its context. It was Cohen who wired the money; the entry’s claim that Trump personally paid it on October 27 is not supported by these sources.

sources.title: April 23, 2020: Task Force Briefing on the Coronavirus Pandemic
The White House Spins Trump’s Disinfectant Remarks

supported_event_claim: During an April 23, 2020 briefing, Trump speculated about whether disinfectant could be applied by injection or ‘almost a cleaning’ and asked whether light could be brought inside the body as a COVID-19 treatment.
reason: The transcript and fact check support the remarks. The packet’s ‘injecting bleach’ phrasing is not a precise quotation, and the asserted nationwide poison-control spike is not supported by these sources.

sources.title: Trump draws scornful rebuke for mocking reporter with disability
Trump mocks disabled reporter

supported_event_claim: At a November 2015 rally, Trump made gestures while discussing New York Times reporter Serge Kovaleski, who has arthrogryposis; contemporaneous video and reporting documented the episode and Kovaleski’s response.
reason: The report and video establish the event. The record’s paraphrase of the movement as a physical imitation is supported by contemporaneous coverage, without inferring motive beyond the documented exchange.

sources.title: Donald Trump calls media ‘the enemy of the American People’
Tweets of February 15, 2017
sources.publisher: The American Presidency Project, UC Santa Barbara

supported_event_claim: Trump repeatedly attacked news organizations as ‘fake news’ and on February 17, 2017, called the news media ‘the enemy of the American People.’
reason: ABC News reports the exact February 17 statement, and the archival tweet collection documents repeated ‘fake news’ language. These sources do not establish the entry’s broader causal claims about danger to journalists or democracy.

sources.title: April 23, 2020: Task Force Briefing on the Coronavirus Pandemic
The White House Spins Trump’s Disinfectant Remarks

supported_event_claim: In the April 23, 2020 briefing, Trump asked about bringing ultraviolet or other powerful light inside the body, including through the skin, as a possible COVID-19 intervention.
reason: The official briefing transcript and contemporaneous fact check directly document the question. The record’s assertion that the idea was ‘medically impossible’ is a characterization rather than the event itself.

sources.title: Trump boards Air Force One with toilet paper in tow. (Or was it a napkin?)
Donald Trump boards Air Force One with paper stuck to his shoe – video

supported_event_claim: On October 4, 2018, video showed paper, described as toilet paper or possibly a napkin, attached to Trump’s shoe as he boarded Air Force One.
reason: The Washington Post and Guardian report the visible paper and provide video-based coverage. Sources do not establish that he was unaware for several minutes or that staff failed to notice.

supported_event_claim: No credible source located supports the packet’s claim that Trump used an autopen to forge his signature on official documents or legislation throughout 2017–2021.
reason: Targeted searches surfaced reporting that autopen use by presidents can be lawful and that Trump later acknowledged limited autopen use for unimportant papers, but no evidence supporting this specific historical allegation. Available sources contradict the implication that autopen use is inherently forgery.

sources.title: AP FACT CHECK: Trump is tilting at wind farms again
Donald Trump’s ridiculous link between cancer, wind turbines

supported_event_claim: At an April 2, 2019 Republican fundraiser, Trump said wind-turbine noise causes cancer; AP reported that this claim was not supported by evidence and cited the American Cancer Society’s lack of credible evidence linking windmill noise and cancer.
reason: Contemporaneous AP coverage and a fact check support the remark and assess the health claim. The source concerns turbine noise, not vibrations as phrased in the packet.

sources.title: VP Vance says meeting with families of victims from Minneapolis church shooting affected him deeply
Vance speaks after meeting with families affected by Minneapolis shooting

supported_event_claim: On September 3, 2025, Vice President JD Vance and Second Lady Usha Vance visited Annunciation Catholic Church in Minneapolis and met with families affected by the August 27 shooting.
reason: The AP and PBS/AP reports directly document the visit, the people present, and its connection to the prior church shooting. The event is not evidence of the unrelated immigration-crackdown category attached to the entry.

sources.title: Epstein survivors demand justice in Washington as Trump calls case ‘a Democrat hoax’
Trump again calls Epstein case a ‘hoax’ as survivors demand accountability

supported_event_claim: On September 3, 2025, Epstein survivors spoke at the Capitol seeking release of investigative files, while Trump called the case a ‘Democrat hoax.’
reason: PBS and AP coverage document both events. No unsupported inference about Trump’s connection to Epstein or the survivors’ allegations is made.

sources.title: Trump threatens ‘Apocalypse Now’-style action against Chicago to boost deportations
Trump threatens Chicago with ‘Department of WAR’ ahead of planned crackdown

supported_event_claim: On September 6, 2025, Trump posted an AI-generated or digitally altered image evoking Apocalypse Now while threatening a federal crackdown and National Guard deployment in Chicago.
reason: NPR and Axios report the post, image, and surrounding threat. The phrasing ‘AI-generated’ is NPR’s characterization; the event itself is directly documented.

sources.title: Conservative activist Charlie Kirk assassinated at Utah university
Conservative activist Charlie Kirk dies after being shot at Utah Valley University event

supported_event_claim: Charlie Kirk was shot and killed while speaking at a Utah Valley University event in Orem on September 10, 2025.
reason: AP reporting and its PBS republication support the event, date, and location. The two links represent the same underlying AP report rather than independent corroboration.

sources.title: President Trump, First Lady Mark 9/11 with Solemn Vow to Never Forget
Remarks on the Anniversary of the September 11, 2001, Terrorist Attacks at the Pentagon

supported_event_claim: President Trump and First Lady Melania Trump attended a September 11, 2025 Pentagon remembrance event and took part in a wreath-laying ceremony.
reason: The White House account and official transcript document the event. They do not support the entry’s assigned violent-rhetoric category, which is unrelated to this visit.

sources.title: Remarks on the Anniversary of the September 11, 2001, Terrorist Attacks at the Pentagon
Trump says he’ll award Charlie Kirk the Presidential Medal of Freedom

supported_event_claim: During remarks at the Pentagon on September 11, 2025, Trump announced he would posthumously award Charlie Kirk the Presidential Medal of Freedom.
reason: The official transcript and CBS report directly document the announcement. The packet’s national-security/war category does not describe this event.
